name: f3-distilled-prereview-defuse-v1
idea_origin: user request 26 Oct: Opus teacher distillation (lab/reports/teacher-digests/distilled-rules.md)
hypothesis: Every Opus game opened with a C, and the most common Opus exit (3 of 6 losses, plus the eliminated Sonnet F3 run) is C, C, D, D. The D after a weak review followed risk that rebuilt once the agent stopped defusing: of 29 reviews that followed a C or D, none of the 7 preceded by Defuse legacy risk in the last Energy phase before the review was a D, against 7 of the 22 without it. In the decisive case (a third review after C, C) the split is 4 of 4 defused and no D versus 4 of 4 not defused and D, within every seed group and within P0 and M3. Adding one line to f3-lean that sets Defuse legacy risk and Prepare report materials in the second Energy phase after any C or D, whatever the signal state, removes that route for Haiku: no D after a weak review in a 4-run screen and mean quantitative_score at least f3-lean's and F3's.
change: Text base f3-lean-v1, unchanged except one line appended to the Weak review plan: 'In the second Energy phase after a C or D, the last before the next review, take Defuse legacy risk and Prepare report materials whatever the signal state.' The line is worded identically in f3-opus-distilled-v1, so that child differs from this one only by the other four distilled rules. No lean line edited. 278 words by wc -w including front matter (f3-lean 250).
predicted_behaviour: In the second Energy phase after every C or D, Energy goes to Defuse legacy risk plus Prepare report materials (Health recovery in place of Prepare report materials only when Health is low), in at least 3 of 4 eligible phases per run, with notes citing the pre-review rule even when the state is Clear. Defuse count per run exceeds f3-lean's by at most the number of weak reviews whose second phase found the state Clear. No D in any review that follows a C or D; capability dismissals 0 of 4. Main actions, story choices and Clear-state Energy otherwise indistinguishable from f3-lean.
refutation: Refuted if, on 4 paired Haiku runs against f3-lean-v1 and f3-feedback-reactive-v1 with the same seeds, (a) a D follows a C or D whose second Energy phase executed the rule, or the share of D grades after weak reviews is not lower than f3-lean's when f3-lean has any, or (b) mean quantitative_score falls below f3-lean's by more than the decision margin (the forced Defuse costs more than it saves). Uninformative rather than refuted if f3-lean's Haiku runs already Defuse in that phase in at least 3 of 4 eligible cases (rule saturated for Haiku; keep it for the DeepSeek screen), or if no arm produces a D. Manipulation fails if the rule is executed in fewer than 3 of 4 eligible phases; then the result says nothing about the rule.
notes: Strongest rule of the Opus distillation (lab/reports/teacher-digests/distilled-rules.md, rule R1), chosen for the most consistent outcome-linked contrast and a visible mechanism: the D reviews cite recent incidents, slips or risk warnings, and in all 7 D grades that followed a weak review the HR remark reached its upper steps within the preceding half-year. Defuse in the FIRST phase after a weak review shows no protection (6 of 12 such cases still ended in D); only the last phase before the review does, which fits risk rebuilding after a step-down. Caveat: Opus's results mix its own capability with the policies it played (F1, P0, M3; never F3); this child tests whether the rule, written for a weaker reader, helps Haiku now and DeepSeek later. Confounds: actor variant (opus~100k won 5 of 6, opus 3 of 8) coincides with the run-id seed group (eaaedd 5 of 6, a10402 2 of 5, d92292 1 of 3); n is small (7 vs 22 reviews). Risk for the screen: f3-lean notes report 11 to 18 Defuse per F3 Haiku run, so Haiku may already defuse in this phase (see refutation). The trigger is relative cadence on the published half-year review and quarterly Energy phases, not a calendar trigger; it reintroduces a signal-free Defuse that f3-lean removed, but only on that cadence after a weak review.
